text: But that he was in no wise prejudiced against the Jews, is indicated in that (1) his whole Memorandum emerged in 1800 in response to the actual misery and hunger of the peasants, (2) the goal was to do well by both the White Russian peasant and the Jews, (3) he distinguished them economically and (4) his desire was to orient the Jews toward a real productive activity, of whom, as Catherine planned, a part first and foremost was supposed to have been relocated in territories that were not closed.

chapter_title: Chapter  3.  During  the  Reign  of  Nicholas  1
text: The first measure against the Jews, which Nicolas considered from the very beginning of his reign, was to put them on an equal footing with the Russian population with regard to the subjugation to compulsory service to the State, and in particular, requiring them to participate physically in conscription, which they had not been subjected to since their attachment to Russia.

beginning  of  his  reign,  was  to  put  them  on  an  equal  footing  with  the  Russian
population  with  regard  to  the  subjugation  to  compulsory  service  to  the  State,
and  in  particular,  requiring  them  to  participate  physically  in  conscription,  which
they  had  not  been  subjected  to  since  their  attachment  to  Russia.

chapter_title: Chapter  3.  During  the  Reign  of  Nicholas  1
text: The bourgeois Jews did not supply recruits, but acquitted 500 rubles per head.208 This measure was not dictated solely by governmental considerations to standardise the obligations of the population (the Jewish communities were in any case very slow to pay the royalties, and moreover, Russia received many Jews from Galicia where they were already required to perform military service); nor by the fact that the obligation to provide recruits â€œwould reduce the number of Jews not engaged in productive workâ€ â€” rather, the idea was that the Jewish recruit, isolated from his closed environment, would be better placed to join the lifestyle of the nation as a whole, and perhaps even orthodoxy.209 Taken into account, these considerations considerably tightened the conditions of the conscription applied to the Jews, leading to a gradual increase in the number of recruits and the lowering of the age of the conscripts.

text: Boris Osipovich Bogdanov (born 1884) was an Odessan, the grandson and son of lumber suppliers.
text_raw:
Boris  Osipovich  Bogdanov  (born  1884)  was  an  Odessan,  the  grandson  and
son  of  lumber  suppliers.

text: He graduated from the best commerce school in Odessa.
text_raw:
He  graduated  from  the  best  commerce  school  in
Odessa.

text: While studying, he joined Social Democrat societies.
text_raw: While  studying,  he  joined  Social  Democrat  societies.

text: In June 1905, he was the first civilian who got on board the mutinous battleship, Potemkin, when she entered the port of Odessa; he gave a speech for her crew, urging sailors to join Odessaâ€™s labor strike; he delivered letters with appeals to consulates of the European powers in Russia.
text_raw:
In  June  1905,  he
was  the  first  civilian  who  got  on  board  the  mutinous  battleship,  Potemkin,  when
she  entered  the  port  of  Odessa;  he  gave  a  speech  for  her  crew,  urging  sailors  to
join  Odessaâ€™s  labor  strike;  he  delivered  letters  with  appeals  to  consulates  of  the
European  powers  in  Russia.

text: He avoided punishment by departing for St. Petersburg where he worked in the Social Democratic underground; he was a Menshevik.
text_raw:
He  avoided  punishment  by  departing  for  St.
Petersburg  where  he  worked  in  the  Social  Democratic  underground;  he  was  a
Menshevik.

text: He was sentenced to two 2-year-long exiles, one after another, to Solvychegodsk and to Vologda.
text_raw:
He  was  sentenced  to  two  2-year-long  exiles,  one  after  another,  to
Solvychegodsk  and  to  Vologda.

text: Before the war, he entered the elite of the Menshevik movement; he worked legally on labor questions.
text_raw:
Before  the  war,  he  entered  the  elite  of  the
Menshevik  movement;  he  worked  legally  on  labor  questions.

text: In 1915 he became the secretary of the Labor Group at the Military Industrial Committee, was arrested in January 1917 and freed by the February Revolution.
text_raw:
In  1915  he
became  the  secretary  of  the  Labor  Group  at  the  Military  Industrial  Committee,
was  arrested  in  January  1917  and  freed  by  the  February  Revolution.

text: He was a member of the Executive Committee of the Soviet of Workersâ€™ and Soldiersâ€™ Deputies of Petrograd, and regularly chaired its noisy sessions which attracted thousands of people.
text_raw:
He  was  a
member  of  the  Executive  Committee  of  the  Soviet  of  Workersâ€™  and  Soldiersâ€™
Deputies  of  Petrograd,  and  regularly  chaired  its  noisy  sessions  which  attracted
thousands  of  people.

text: From June 1917 he was a member of the Bureau of the All-Russian Central Executive Committee and persistently opposed ongoing attempts of the Bolsheviks to seize power.
text_raw:
From  June  1917  he  was  a  member  of  the  Bureau  of  the
All-Russian  Central  Executive  Committee  and  persistently  opposed  ongoing
attempts  of  the  Bolsheviks  to  seize  power.

text: After the failed Bolshevik rebellion in July 1917 he accepted the surrender of the squad of sailors besieged in the Petropavlovsk Fortress.
text_raw:
After  the  failed  Bolshevik  rebellion
in  July  1917  he  accepted  the  surrender  of  the  squad  of  sailors  besieged  in  the
Petropavlovsk  Fortress.

text: After the October coup, in 1918 he was one of the organizers of anti-Bolshevik workers movement in Petrograd.
text_raw:
After  the  October  coup,  in  1918  he  was  one  of  the
organizers  of  anti-Bolshevik  workers  movement  in  Petrograd.

text: During the Civil War he lived in Odessa.
text_raw:
During  the  Civil
War  he  lived  in  Odessa.

After  the  Civil  War  he  tried  to  restart  the  Menshevik
political  activity,  but  at  the  end  of  1920  he  was  arrested  for  one  year.

the  beginning  of  many  years  of  unceasing  arrests  and  sentences,  exiles  and

text: In 1990, while finishing April 1917 and sorting out the enormous amount of material not included in The Red Wheel, I decided to present some of that material in the form of a historical essay about Jews in the Russian revolution.
text_raw:
In  1990,  while  finishing  April  1917  and  sorting  out  the  enormous  amount  of
material  not  included  in  The  Red  Wheel,  I  decided  to  present  some  of  that
material  in  the  form  of  a  historical  essay  about  Jews  in  the  Russian  revolution.

text: Yet it became clear almost immediately that in order to understand those events the essay must step back in time.
text_raw:
Yet  it  became  clear  almost  immediately  that  in  order  to  understand  those
events  the  essay  must  step  back  in  time.

text: Thus, it stepped back to the very first incorporation of the Jews into the Russian Empire in 1772.
text_raw:
Thus,  it  stepped  back  to  the  very  first
incorporation  of  the  Jews  into  the  Russian  Empire  in  1772.

text: On the other hand, the revolution of 1917 provided a powerful impetus to Russian Jewry, so the essay naturally stretched into the post-revolutionary period.
text_raw:
On  the  other  hand,
the  revolution  of  1917  provided  a  powerful  impetus  to  Russian  Jewry,  so  the
essay  naturally  stretched  into  the  post-revolutionary  period.

text: Thus, the title Two Hundred Years Together was born.
text_raw:
Thus,  the  title  Two
Hundred  Years  Together  was  born.

text: However, it took time for me to realize the importance of that distinct historical boundary drawn by mass emigration of the Jews from the Soviet Union that had begun in the 1970s (exactly 200 years after the Jews appeared in Russia) and which had become unrestricted by 1987.
text_raw:
However,  it  took  time  for  me  to  realize  the  importance  of  that  distinct
historical  boundary  drawn  by  mass  emigration  of  the  Jews  from  the  Soviet
Union  that  had  begun  in  the  1970s  (exactly  200  years  after  the  Jews  appeared  in
Russia)  and  which  had  become  unrestricted  by  1987.

text: This boundary had been abolished, so that for the first time, the non-voluntary status of the Russian Jews no longer a fact: they ought not to live here anymore;
Israel waits for them; all countries of the world are open to them.
text_raw:
Israel  waits  for  them;  all
countries  of  the  world  are  open  to  them.

text: This clear boundary changed my intention to keep the narrative up to the mid-1990s, because the message of the book was already played out: the uniqueness of Russian-Jewish entwinement disappeared at the moment of the new Exodus.
text_raw:
This  clear  boundary  changed  my
intention  to  keep  the  narrative  up  to  the  mid-1990s,  because  the  message  of  the
book  was  already  played  out:  the  uniqueness  of  Russian-Jewish  entwinement
disappeared  at  the  moment  of  the  new  Exodus.

text: Now, a totally new period in the history of the by-now-free Russian Jewry and its relations with the new Russia began.

and  its  relations  with  the  new  Russia  began.

text: This period started with swift and essential changes, but it is still too early to predict its long-term outcomes and judge whether its peculiar Russian-Jewish character will persevere or it will be supplanted with the universal laws of the Jewish Diaspora.
